# Mermaid API

Download OpenAPI Document Download OpenAPI Document

Mermaid API validates and renders Mermaid diagrams for programs: agents, LLM tool calls, CI pipelines and products. Validate says whether diagram code is valid and why not; render turns it into SVG, PNG or PDF, with the latest Mermaid unless the call pins an earlier one; generate asks Mermaid AI for diagram code from a prompt, and repair asks it to fix invalid code. The operations below are the contract; this guide is what they do not say by themselves. Mermaid API is part of Mermaid; keys are created in the console. Agents: llms.txt lists every document.

## Beta

Mermaid API is in beta. Request and response fields may be added, renamed or removed; defaults, limits and ceilings may move; the latest Mermaid version bumps without notice, so the same code may render differently over time unless the call pins a version. What does not change: the `/v1` prefix, the error structure, every error code once shipped, and bearer authentication. Breaking changes are announced, not versioned: each is listed in the changelog at the end of this guide with its date and what a caller must do. Every response carries `x-mermaid-api-phase: beta` until general availability. Do not build a production dependency on it yet.

## Authentication

Every `/v1` call except the reference endpoints needs an API key: `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Keys are created in the console by any Mermaid Chart user, shown once at creation, and have no expiry by default. A key is `<prefix>.<secret>`, the prefix `mmd_` and twelve hex digits; the prefix appears in listings, the secret is stored only as a hash. A refused key is 401 with `www-authenticate: Bearer` and one of `ERR_KEY_MISSING`, `ERR_KEY_UNKNOWN`, `ERR_KEY_REVOKED`, `ERR_KEY_EXPIRED`: fix the key, do not retry. `ERR_KEY_OWNER_DELETED` means Mermaid Chart no longer knows the key's owner: the key works again once it does, within 5 minutes. The examples below take the key from `$MERMAID_API_KEY`.

## Validate

`POST /v1/validate`, a valid diagram:
    
    `curl -s "https://api.mermaid.ai/v1/validate" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $MERMAID_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"code": "flowchart TD\n  A[Start] --> B[Done]"}'
    `
    
    `{ "valid": true, "diagramType": "flowchart-v2" }
    `

## Render

`POST /v1/render` in bytes mode, a PNG written to a file:
    
    `curl -s "https://api.mermaid.ai/v1/render" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $MERMAID_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -o diagram.png \
      -d '{"code": "flowchart TD\n  A[Start] --> B[Done]", "format": "png", "png": {"scale": 2, "background": "white"}}'
    `

JSON mode, an SVG with a Mermaid config:
    
    `curl -s "https://api.mermaid.ai/v1/render" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $MERMAID_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -H "Accept: application/json" \
      -d '{"code": "flowchart TD\n  A[Start] --> B[Done]", "format": "svg", "config": {"theme": "forest"}}'
    `
    
    `{ "format": "svg", "contentType": "image/svg+xml", "content": "PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0i...", "diagramType": "flowchart-v2", "mermaidVersion": "12.1.0", "requestId": "req-3f2a9c1b7d4e", "cacheStatus": "miss" }
    `

An invalid diagram, answered 400:
    
    `curl -s "https://api.mermaid.ai/v1/render" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $MERMAID_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"code": "flowchart TD\n  A --> B\n  C ==>> D", "format": "svg"}'
    `
    
    `{ "error": { "code": "ERR_DIAGRAM_INVALID", "message": "Parse error on line 3:\n...TD  A --> B  C ==>> D\n---------------------^\nExpecting 'AMP', 'COLON', ..., got 'TAGEND'", "details": { "name": "Error", "line": 3, "column": 4 } } }
    `

## Generate

`POST /v1/generate`, one diagram from a prompt, checked with Mermaid's parser before it is returned:
    
    `curl -s "https://api.mermaid.ai/v1/generate" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $MERMAID_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"prompt": "Alice says hello to Bob, as a sequence diagram"}'
    `
    
    `{ "valid": true, "code": "sequenceDiagram\n  Alice->>Bob: Hello", "diagramType": "sequence" }
    `

## Response headers

Header  | On  | Meaning
--- | --- | ---
`x-request-id`  | every response  | The request id; quote it when reporting a problem. A caller-supplied one (6 to 48 letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `=`) is echoed.
`x-mermaid-api-phase`  | every response  | The release phase, `beta` during the beta.
`ratelimit-policy`  | every response for an accepted key  | The burst limit in force, an IETF RateLimit field: `"burst";q=<limit>;w=<window seconds>`. Absent while the burst limit is not being enforced.
`ratelimit`  | every response for an accepted key  | Where the call stands against it: `"burst";r=<remaining>;t=<seconds to reset>`. Absent with the policy.
`retry-after`  | 429, and a 402 the allowance's reset will cover  | Seconds to wait before the next call.
`www-authenticate`  | 401  | `Bearer`: the scheme the endpoint takes.
`content-type`  | every JSON body  | `application/json`.

## Render cache

A render identical to a recent one is served from the render cache: same diagram code, effective Mermaid config, format, format options and Mermaid version. Send `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.  |  | 
`ERR_KEY_UNKNOWN`  | 401  | No key with that prefix exists, or the secret is wrong. Check the key was copied whole.  |  | 
`ERR_KEY_REVOKED`  | 401  | The key was revoked by its owner or a super admin. A super admin, or an admin of the organisation owning it, can restore it; otherwise create a new key in the console.  |  | 
`ERR_KEY_EXPIRED`  | 401  | The key is past its expiry. Create a new key in the console.  |  | 
`ERR_KEY_OWNER_DELETED`  | 401  | Mermaid Chart no longer knows the account or organisation owning the key. Nothing is charged and the key is kept: it works again, within 5 minutes, once Mermaid Chart knows its owner again.  |  | 
`ERR_IDENTITY_MISSING`  | 401  | Console endpoints only: no Mermaid Chart token was forwarded. Not returned under `/v1`.  |  | 
`ERR_IDENTITY_INVALID`  | 401  | Console endpoints only: Mermaid Chart rejected the forwarded token. Not returned under `/v1`.  |  | 
`ERR_IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE`  | 503  | Console endpoints only: Mermaid Chart could not be asked about the token; retry later.

# Authentication

MERMAID uses OAuth2 authentication for securing and accessing the MERMAID API's secure endpoints. The following steps are required before making requests to the API:

## 1. Create a MERMAID Account

Before you can make a request for a JSON Web Token (JWT) or accessing the API, you must first create a MERMAID user account. If you already have an account jump to section 2, if not, an account can be created at https://app.datamermaid.org/.

## 2. Requesting Tokens

OAuth2 Implicit grant type is used to fetch a valid token that can be used to securely access MERMAID API. The folowing details will be needed to setup an implicit authorization flow:

>   * Authorization URL
>   * Redirect URL
>   * Client ID
>   * Audience

These details can be requested from the MERMAID team at https://datamermaid.org/contact-us/.

## 3. Calling API

When making requests to the API the token can be included in:

  * the request header
    
    curl --request GET \
        --url https://api.datamermaid.org/projects/ \
        --header 'Authorization: Bearer <VALID TOKEN HERE>'
    

  * the url query string
    
    https://api.datamermaid.org/projects/?access_token=<VALID TOKEN HERE>

## Mermaid is open source. Why use the API?

Nothing to host

Rendering Mermaid needs a headless browser. We run it, so you send one HTTP request.

Always the latest Mermaid

Including Mermaid's own layouts and themes, the day they ship.

Answers a program can use

Stable error codes with line and column, not a stack trace.

Built by the Mermaid team

The people who make Mermaid run the service.

## Built for programs, not people

Self-describing

An OpenAPI document and an llms.txt, so agents and code generators can find their own way around.

Stable error codes

Every failure has a documented code that will not change. Messages may improve; codes stay.

Pin your Mermaid version

Choose the Mermaid version a call uses, so a render does not change under you.

Know your balance

A free endpoint tells your program what it has left and what each call costs. Out of credits says "buy"; too fast says "wait".

## FAQ

Have questions about Mermaid API? These should help.

Contact sales

What is Mermaid API, and how is it different from Mermaid?

Mermaid is the open-source language and library that turns text into diagrams. Mermaid API is a hosted service that runs Mermaid for you: your program sends diagram code over HTTP and gets back a validation result, an image, or new diagram code.

Do I need a Mermaid subscription?

No. Any Mermaid account works, including a free one, and every account gets a monthly allowance of API credits. Paid plans include a bigger allowance.

How does pricing work?

Each call costs a set number of API credits. Your monthly allowance is spent first, then any credits you have bought. Costs are published in the docs, and a free endpoint tells your program what it has left. For high volume, contact sales.

Which diagram types and output formats are supported?

Every diagram type Mermaid supports (see the docs). Images come as SVG, PNG or PDF.

What happens to my diagram code?

We don't store it. Rendered images are cached for up to a day so a repeated request is fast, and you can turn caching off per request. Our usage records hold counts and sizes, never your diagrams.

Can I pin a Mermaid version?

Yes. Each call can name the Mermaid version it should use, so your output stays the same until you choose to upgrade.

Is it production-ready?

Mermaid API is in open beta. You can build on it; breaking changes are announced in advance in the changelog, and there is no uptime guarantee yet.

Where are the docs?

At api.mermaid.ai/v1/docs, with examples, an OpenAPI document and an llms.txt for agents.
